title: The Reading 7-1 Practice Questions
instructions: 10 questions for each unit · 5 choices · Choose one answer for each question.

items.title: [1–10] Read the passage and answer the questions.
items.text:
Throughout time, art has been used to ⟪decorate⟫ homes, churches, and public buildings. In modern times, art is used in advertisements, magazines, cartoons, and even on television! Art in advertisements has become increasingly popular. ⟪This⟫ is called commercial art. One of the most famous commercial artists was Andy Warhol.

Andy Warhol was often sick as a child, so he spent a lot of time drawing. After college, he began his ⟪career⟫ making art for advertisements. His drawings of shoes became so well known that people wanted to see more of his work. Thus, in the 1950s, he began showing his popular works in art galleries. Warhol was one of the first artists to use silkscreen ink printing in his work. During the 1960s, he produced many famous art pieces depicting everyday objects. These include Coca-Cola bottles, dollar bills, and Campbell’s Soup cans. This kind of art is referred to as “pop art.”

Some critics think Andy Warhol was only interested in making money with his art. ⟪Others⟫ thought he was the perfect example of commercialized modern life. Apart from this argument, most critics agree that Warhol’s work shows the changing value of art in everyday life.
items.note: Words: increasingly = more and more · advertisement = a picture or words that tell people to buy something · silkscreen ink printing = a way of printing pictures · depict = show, draw · critic = a person who gives opinions about art · commercialized = made to make money · argument = a disagreement

items.prompt: What does the underlined word ⟪decorate⟫ mean?
items.explanation: [난이도 1·매우 쉬움 / 어휘(단어 뜻)] decorate(장식하다) = make something look nicer. 집·교회·공공건물을 ‘꾸미는’ 데 미술이 쓰여 왔다는 문맥이다.

items.prompt: What does the underlined word ⟪career⟫ mean?
choices: the job a person does for a long time
the house a person lives in
the school a person goes to
items.explanation: [난이도 1·매우 쉬움 / 어휘(단어 뜻)] career(경력, 직업) = the job a person does for a long time. 대학을 마친 뒤 광고 미술을 하며 ‘직업 생활’을 시작했다는 문맥이다.

items.prompt: According to the passage, when did Warhol begin showing his works in art galleries?
items.explanation: [난이도 2·쉬움 / 세부 사실] Thus, in the 1950s, he began showing his popular works in art galleries. 1960년대는 일상 사물을 그린 작품을 만든 시기이다.

items.prompt: According to the passage, Warhol was one of the first artists to use ______.
items.explanation: [난이도 2·쉬움 / 세부 사실] Warhol was one of the first artists to use silkscreen ink printing in his work.

items.prompt: What does the underlined word ⟪This⟫ refer to?
items.explanation: [난이도 3·보통 / 지칭 추론] 바로 앞 문장 Art in advertisements has become increasingly popular. 를 받아 ‘이것(광고 속 미술)’을 commercial art라고 부른다고 했다.

items.prompt: What does the underlined word ⟪Others⟫ refer to?
items.explanation: [난이도 3·보통 / 지칭 추론] 앞 문장 Some critics think … 에 이어 Others thought … 이므로 ‘다른 비평가들’이다. 뒤에 most critics agree로 비평가 이야기가 이어진다.

items.prompt: Which is the correct order of (A), (B), and (C), from first to last?
items.explanation: [난이도 4·다소 어려움 / 사건 순서 배열] 어릴 때 그림을 많이 그림(B) → 대학 졸업 후 광고 미술 일을 시작(C) → 신발 그림이 유명해져 사람들이 작품을 더 보고 싶어 함(A). 2문단의 순서 그대로이다.
items.box:
(A) Many people wanted to see more of Warhol’s work. \
(B) Warhol spent a lot of time drawing as a child. \
(C) Warhol got his first job making art for advertisements.

items.prompt: Which is *NOT* true according to the passage?
choices: Art has been used to decorate churches.
Some critics think Warhol only wanted to make money with his art.
Warhol’s drawings of shoes were not well known.
Warhol made art pieces of Campbell’s Soup cans.
Most critics agree that Warhol’s work shows the changing value of art.
items.explanation: [난이도 4·다소 어려움 / 내용 불일치] His drawings of shoes became so well known that people wanted to see more of his work — 신발 그림은 ‘매우 유명해졌다’고 했으므로 ‘유명하지 않았다’는 틀리다. 나머지는 decorate … churches / Some critics think … making money / Campbell’s Soup cans / most critics agree … 와 일치한다.

items.prompt: What can we learn from the passage?
choices: Warhol made art only for television.
Warhol’s works were shown only in art galleries.
People in the past did not use art to decorate buildings.
Critics have different ideas about why Warhol made his art.
items.explanation: [난이도 5·어려움 / 추론] Some critics think … Others thought … Apart from this argument — 비평가들의 생각이 서로 달랐다. Warhol은 광고 미술을 만들고 미술관에서도 전시했으므로 TV만을 위해 만든 것도, 미술관에서만 보인 것도 아니고, 옛날에도 미술로 건물을 꾸몄으며, 대학 졸업 후에도 계속 그림을 그렸다.

items.prompt: What can we learn from the passage?
choices: Pop art used pictures of things people saw every day.
Pop art showed pictures of homes and churches.
Pop art showed mostly famous people.
Pop art was the first kind of art Warhol made.
Most critics think pop art was only about making money.
items.explanation: [난이도 5·어려움 / 추론] many famous art pieces depicting everyday objects … This kind of art is referred to as “pop art.” — 일상 사물(콜라병, 지폐, 수프 캔)을 그린 작품이 팝 아트이다. 집이나 교회, 유명인이 아니라 사물을 그렸고, Warhol은 어릴 때 그림을 그리고 광고 미술을 거친 뒤 1960년대에 팝 아트를 만들었으며, 대부분의 비평가는 그의 작품이 ‘미술의 달라진 가치’를 보여 준다고 본다.

items.title: [1–10] Read the passage and answer the questions.
items.text:
The water cycle is ⟪necessary⟫ for life on Earth. Water on the ground evaporates into vapor and forms clouds in the sky. In return, rain brings water back down to the ground again, which ends up in streams, rivers, lakes, and oceans. What happens when humans tamper with the water cycle?

Most evaporation ⟪occurs⟫ in oceans as a result of the Sun’s energy. This cools the temperature of Earth’s climate and also affects the oceans’ salt content. Having the correct amount of salt in the oceans maintains a delicate ecosystem of plants, fish, and other wildlife. One example of a disaster caused by tampering with the water cycle is the drying-up of the Aral Sea. The two rivers that fed the Aral Sea were diverted for farming in the desert. As a result, the sea is now almost completely dry, killing the wildlife that lived there and causing dust storms that affect human health.

As we can see, the water cycle is necessary to keep the environment balanced. It is important to understand the water cycle and to protect our water sources so they can function well for Earth’s sake.
items.note: Words: evaporate = change into gas · evaporation = when water evaporates · vapor = water in the air · in return = then, the other way · end up = finally arrive · tamper with = change something in a bad way · climate = the usual weather of a place · temperature = how hot or cold something is · affect = change something · salt content = the amount of salt · delicate = easily hurt or broken · ecosystem = all the living things in a place · wildlife = wild animals and plants · disaster = a very bad event · fed = brought water to · divert = make a river go a different way · dust storm = a strong wind full of dust · function = work · for Earth’s sake = for the good of Earth

items.prompt: Which can best replace the underlined word ⟪occurs⟫?
items.explanation: [난이도 1·매우 쉬움 / 문맥상 동의어] occur = happen(일어나다). 증발은 대부분 바다에서 ‘일어난다’는 뜻이다.

items.prompt: Which can best replace the underlined word ⟪necessary⟫?
items.explanation: [난이도 1·매우 쉬움 / 문맥상 동의어] necessary = needed(꼭 필요한). 물의 순환은 지구의 생명에 ‘꼭 필요하다’. 마지막 문단에서도 같은 단어가 쓰였다.

items.prompt: According to the passage, what causes most evaporation in the oceans?
items.explanation: [난이도 2·쉬움 / 세부 사실] Most evaporation occurs in oceans as a result of the Sun’s energy. — 태양의 에너지 때문이다.

items.prompt: According to the passage, where does rainwater end up?
items.explanation: [난이도 2·쉬움 / 세부 사실] rain brings water back down to the ground again, which ends up in streams, rivers, lakes, and oceans.

items.prompt: Why does the writer talk about dust storms?
choices: to explain how clouds are made
to explain how the Sun warms the oceans
to describe the weather in the ocean
to show that the dry Aral Sea hurts people’s health
to explain why the sea is salty
items.explanation: [난이도 3·보통 / 언급 이유] … causing dust storms that affect human health — 바다가 마른 결과로 생긴 모래 폭풍이 사람의 건강을 해친다는 것을 보여 주기 위해서이다.

items.prompt: Why does the writer talk about the salt in the oceans?
choices: to show that sea life needs the right amount of salt
to explain why seawater tastes bad to drink
to show how people make salt from the sea
to explain why fish die in rivers and lakes
to show how clouds get their water from the sea
items.explanation: [난이도 3·보통 / 언급 이유] Having the correct amount of salt in the oceans maintains a delicate ecosystem of plants, fish, and other wildlife — 알맞은 소금 양이 있어야 바다 생물의 생태계가 지켜진다는 뜻이다.

items.prompt: Which is *NOT* true according to the passage?
choices: Water on the ground evaporates and forms clouds.
Evaporation changes the amount of salt in the oceans.
There are plants, fish, and other wildlife in the oceans.
People can change the water cycle in a bad way.
Rain takes water from the ground up to the sky.
items.explanation: [난이도 4·다소 어려움 / 내용 불일치] rain brings water back down to the ground — 비는 물을 하늘에서 땅으로 ‘내려’ 보낸다. 물을 하늘로 올리는 것은 증발이다. 나머지는 evaporates into vapor and forms clouds / affects the oceans’ salt content / ecosystem of plants, fish, and other wildlife / humans tamper with the water cycle 와 일치한다.

items.prompt: Which is true according to the passage?
choices: The Aral Sea dried up because there was too little rain.
It is important to understand the water cycle.
Dust storms made the Aral Sea dry.
The two rivers still flow into the Aral Sea.
items.explanation: [난이도 4·다소 어려움 / 내용 일치] It is important to understand the water cycle and to protect our water sources. Aral Sea는 비가 적어서가 아니라 강물을 다른 곳으로 돌려서 말랐고(diverted), 모래 폭풍은 바다가 마른 ‘결과’이며, 두 강은 이제 바다로 흐르지 않고, 구름은 증발한 수증기로 만들어진다(evaporates into vapor and forms clouds).

items.prompt:
Complete the summary of the passage. Which words best fit (A) and (B)?

The Aral Sea became dry. This (A) ______ the animals that lived there and (B) ______ dust storms.
items.explanation: [난이도 5·어려움 / 요약문 완성] the sea is now almost completely dry, killing the wildlife that lived there and causing dust storms — 바다가 마르면서 그곳의 동물들이 ‘죽었고(killed)’ 모래 폭풍이 ‘생겼다(caused)’. 동물을 돕거나 옮겼다는 내용, 모래 폭풍을 막았다는 내용은 없다.

items.prompt:
Complete the summary of the passage. Which words best fit (A) and (B)?

Evaporation keeps Earth from getting too (A) ______. The right amount of salt in the oceans helps the plants and fish in the sea (B) ______.
items.explanation: [난이도 5·어려움 / 요약문 완성] (A) This cools the temperature of Earth’s climate — 증발이 기후를 ‘식히므로’ 지구가 너무 ‘더워지지(hot)’ 않게 막는다. 지문의 cools만 보고 cold를 고르면 뜻이 반대가 된다. (B) maintains a delicate ecosystem of plants, fish, and other wildlife — 알맞은 소금 양 덕분에 바다 생물이 ‘살(live)’ 수 있다.

items.title: [1–10] Read the passage and answer the questions.
items.text:
In the 1980s, people who protested the increasing trend of fast food started a “slow food” movement. The movement aimed to preserve local foods, recipes, and communities, while (a) ______ fast, commercialized foods. This inspired the “slow city movement.”

The first Slow City was Chianti, Italy. The people there wanted to keep nature in good shape and protect historic buildings. They came up with a plan for developing their town just the way they wanted. ⟪They⟫ called this plan cittaslow. The term comes from the words “slow” and “citta,” which means “town” or “city” in Italian. The founders of this plan decided that new developments should keep people healthy and promote good relationships among neighbors. They also thought development should not (b) ______ the natural environment.

Since 1999, dozens of cities around the world have been named Slow Cities. They have a lot of green places where people can exercise and enjoy nature. Slow Cities do not have many fast-food restaurants or big supermarkets. Instead, they have locally owned restaurants and small markets. Try visiting a Slow City someday to see if you like it!
items.note: Words: protest = say no to something · trend = what many people do · preserve = keep · commercialized = made to make money · inspire = give an idea · historic = old and important · come up with = think of · term = a word · founder = a person who starts something · promote = help something grow · dozens of = many · exercise = move your body to stay healthy · locally owned = owned by people in the town

items.prompt: According to the passage, when did the slow food movement start?
items.explanation: [난이도 1·매우 쉬움 / 세부 사실] In the 1980s, people who protested the increasing trend of fast food started a “slow food” movement.

items.prompt: According to the passage, what does “citta” mean in Italian?
items.explanation: [난이도 1·매우 쉬움 / 세부 사실] “citta,” which means “town” or “city” in Italian.

items.prompt: Which word best fits in blank (a)?
items.explanation: [난이도 2·쉬움 / 문장 빈칸 어휘] 패스트푸드의 유행에 반대한(protested) 사람들이 시작한 운동이 지역 음식을 지키면서 패스트푸드를 ‘거부했다(rejecting)’는 흐름이다. 패스트푸드를 사거나 먹는다는 것은 운동의 취지와 반대이다.

items.prompt: Which word best fits in blank (b)?
items.explanation: [난이도 2·쉬움 / 문장 빈칸 어휘] 앞 문장에서 새 개발은 사람을 건강하게 하고 이웃 관계를 좋게 해야 한다고 했고, 2문단 첫머리에서 자연을 좋은 상태로 지키고 싶어 했다고 했다. 따라서 개발은 자연환경을 ‘해치지(hurt)’ 않아야 한다.

items.prompt: What is paragraph 2 mainly about?
choices: the history of fast food in Italy
the first Slow City and its plan
how to visit a Slow City
items.explanation: [난이도 3·보통 / 문단 주제] 2문단은 최초의 슬로시티 Chianti와 그곳 사람들이 세운 계획 cittaslow의 뜻과 원칙을 설명한다.

items.prompt: What does the underlined word ⟪They⟫ refer to?
choices: the people who started the slow food movement
items.explanation: [난이도 3·보통 / 지칭 추론] 2문단의 They는 앞 문장들의 주어 The people there(= Chianti 사람들)를 가리킨다. 그들이 마을 개발 계획을 세우고 cittaslow라고 불렀다. 슬로푸드 운동을 시작한 사람들(1문단), 패스트푸드를 좋아하는 사람들, 대형 마트 주인, 관광객은 2문단에 나오지 않는다.

items.prompt: Which is true according to the passage?
choices: Slow Cities have many big supermarkets.
People in Slow Cities can exercise outdoors in nature.
The slow city movement started before the slow food movement.
People in Chianti wanted to build many new fast-food restaurants.
Two cities have been named Slow Cities since 1999.
items.explanation: [난이도 4·다소 어려움 / 내용 일치] They have a lot of green places where people can exercise and enjoy nature. 슬로시티에는 대형 마트가 많지 않고, 슬로푸드 운동이 먼저였으며(This inspired …), Chianti 사람들은 자연과 역사적 건물을 지키려 했고, ‘수십 개(dozens of)’ 도시가 지정되었다.

items.prompt: Which is *NOT* true according to the passage?
choices: People in Chianti wanted to keep nature in good shape.
Cittaslow was a plan for developing the town.
Slow Cities have locally owned restaurants.
New developments in Chianti did not need to keep people healthy.
The slow food movement wanted to keep local foods and recipes.
items.explanation: [난이도 4·다소 어려움 / 내용 불일치] new developments should keep people healthy — 새 개발은 사람을 건강하게 ‘해야 한다’고 했으므로, 건강을 지킬 필요가 없었다는 것은 틀리다. 나머지는 keep nature in good shape / a plan for developing their town / locally owned restaurants / preserve local foods, recipes 와 일치한다.

items.prompt: Which place would you most likely find in a Slow City?
choices: a small market owned by a family in the town
a street with many fast-food restaurants
a factory that makes the river dirty
a new road built over a green park
items.explanation: [난이도 5·어려움 / 추론·적용] 슬로시티에는 패스트푸드점과 대형 마트가 많지 않고, 대신 지역 주민이 소유한 식당과 작은 시장(locally owned restaurants and small markets)이 있다. 강을 더럽히는 공장은 ‘개발은 자연환경을 해치지 않아야 한다’는 원칙에, 녹지 위의 새 도로는 ‘녹지가 많고 자연을 좋은 상태로 지킨다’는 내용에 어긋난다.

items.prompt: What can we learn from the passage?
choices: Slow Cities have more fast-food restaurants than other cities.
There are Slow Cities in many countries now.
People in Slow Cities cannot buy food in their own town.
Slow Cities have no plan for new developments.
Slow Cities do not care about nature.
items.explanation: [난이도 5·어려움 / 추론] Since 1999, dozens of cities around the world have been named Slow Cities — 슬로시티가 세계 여러 나라에 있음을 알 수 있다. 슬로시티에는 패스트푸드점이 많지 않고, 작은 시장과 지역 식당이 있으며, cittaslow라는 개발 계획이 있고, 자연을 좋은 상태로 지키며 녹지가 많다.

items.title: [1–10] Read the passage and answer the questions.
items.text:
Before modern chemistry, ⟪ancient⟫ people tried to understand the makeup of the world. The ancient Greek philosopher Empedocles theorized that four elements made up every substance known to man. These elements were water, fire, earth, and air.

What observations did Empedocles make about these elements? First, he noted that pots were made with earth and water. After being mixed and shaped, they were burned with fire and cooled with air. All four elements were necessary to (a) ______. The same pot was used for cooking plants from the earth, often mixed with water, over a flame. The air cooled down the food so it could be eaten. Thus, all four elements were necessary to prepare a meal. Empedocles also believed that these elements were indestructible and unchangeable. His theories inspired later scientists to study more about the elements that make up our world.

Think about your life and all of your ⟪belongings⟫. How are the four elements involved in things you own, such as your computer, your clothes, and the food you eat? Thinking about everyday objects on a small scale can help us (b) ______.
items.note: Words: chemistry = the science of what things are made of · makeup = what something is made of · philosopher = a person who thinks about big questions · theorize / theory = an idea about how something works · element = a basic thing that makes up everything · substance = a thing, a material · known to man = that people know about · observation = what you see · note = see, notice · flame = fire · thus = so · necessary = needed · prepare = make ready · inspire = give someone new ideas · involved in = a part of · everyday objects = things we use every day · on a small scale = by looking at small things

items.prompt: According to the passage, who was Empedocles?
items.explanation: [난이도 1·매우 쉬움 / 세부 사실] The ancient Greek philosopher Empedocles theorized that …

items.prompt: According to the passage, who did Empedocles’s theories inspire?
items.explanation: [난이도 1·매우 쉬움 / 세부 사실] His theories inspired later scientists to study more about the elements that make up our world.

items.prompt: What does the underlined word ⟪ancient⟫ mean?
items.explanation: [난이도 2·쉬움 / 어휘(단어 뜻)] ancient(고대의) = very old. ‘현대 화학 이전(Before modern chemistry)’의 옛날 사람들을 가리킨다.

items.prompt: What does the underlined word ⟪belongings⟫ mean?
items.explanation: [난이도 2·쉬움 / 어휘(단어 뜻)] belongings(소지품) = things that you own. 바로 뒤에 things you own, such as your computer, your clothes 라고 풀어 말한다.

items.prompt: Complete the table about the passage. Which words best fit (A) and (B)?
items.explanation: [난이도 3·보통 / 도표 완성] cooking plants from the earth, often mixed with water, over a flame — 식물은 ‘물(water)’과 섞고, ‘불꽃(flame)’ 위에서 요리하므로 (A) water, (B) fire. flame을 fire로 바꿔 읽어야 한다.
table: The plants are mixed with it.
The plants are cooked over it.

items.prompt:
Complete the summary of the passage. Which words best fit (A) and (B)?

Empedocles saw that making a pot needs all (A) ______ elements, and he believed that the elements could not be (B) ______.
items.explanation: [난이도 3·보통 / 요약문 완성] (A) All four elements were necessary to make one pot — 네(four) 원소가 모두 필요했다. (B) these elements were indestructible and unchangeable — 변할(changed) 수 없다. un-(아닌) + change(변하다) + -able(할 수 있는).

items.prompt: What is paragraph 2 mainly about?
choices: how to make a strong pot at home
why fire is dangerous when we cook
the four elements in making pots and meals

items.title: [1–10] Read the passage and answer the questions.
items.text:
How did the teddy bear get its name? It comes from U.S. president Theodore Roosevelt. During a hunting trip, Roosevelt refused to kill a bear that had been tied to a tree. All over America, people heard about this story. Some people even made stuffed bears and called ⟪them⟫ “teddy bears” in honor of the president’s ⟪nickname⟫, Teddy.

Teddy bears became mass-produced in the twentieth century. ⟪They⟫ were mainly toys for children, but they were also popularly featured in books and even in movies. Some well-known examples include Winnie the Pooh, which was originally written for adults, as well as Paddington Bear. Due to their popularity, teddy bears were manufactured in a wide range of sizes, colors, and materials. They have endured such lasting popularity that there are museums dedicated to teddy bears all around the world. England, Japan, and South Korea are just a few countries that have teddy bear museums.

Whether they are children’s toys, subjects of books, or objects on display at museums, teddy bears remain popular. They bring children ⟪comfort⟫ and are fun to play with. Teddy bears will probably be around for a long time to come.
items.note: Words: refuse = say no · stuffed bear = a toy bear · in honor of = to show respect for · mass-produced = made in large numbers · be featured in = appear in · manufacture = make · endure = last a long time · dedicated to = made for · subject = what a book is about

items.title: [1–10] Read the passage and answer the questions.
items.text:
Molecules are always moving. Sometimes, molecules even move through membranes. Molecules tend to pass through semi-permeable membranes to an area where the solvent concentration is higher. This equalizes the concentration of materials on either side of the membrane. This process is called osmosis. Osmosis is an important chemical process with ⟪practical⟫ uses in everyday life. What is one use of osmosis?

Fresh vegetables have a high concentration of water molecules. During pickling, vegetables are placed in a brine—a mixture of water, salt, and seasonings. The skin acts as a semi-permeable membrane. Water molecules move out of the vegetables through the skin and into the brine, which equalizes the solvent concentration on either side of the membrane. This process is an example of osmosis, and it is why pickled vegetables stay crunchy.

Reverse osmosis is a process that uses pressure to ⟪force⟫ molecules into an area of lower solute concentration. We use reverse osmosis to remove salt and other particles from seawater. Afterward, we can drink the water!

Chemical processes like osmosis have a big effect on our everyday lives. For this reason, learning about how they work is important for our understanding of the world.
items.note: Words: molecule = a very small part of a thing · tend to = usually · membrane = a thin skin · semi-permeable membrane = a skin that lets only some things pass · solvent = the liquid (here, water) · solute = the thing in the liquid (here, salt) · concentration = how much of something is in a liquid · equalize = make equal · on either side of = on both sides of · process = the way something happens, step by step · chemical = about how things mix and change · pickling = making pickles · seasonings = things you add to food for taste · crunchy = hard, not soft · reverse = the other way around · pressure = pressing hard on something · particle = a very small piece · effect = a change that something makes

(B) force molecules into an area of lower solute concentration — 용질(solute)이 ‘더 적은(less)’ 쪽으로 밀어 넣는다. 단어 풀이의 solvent·solute 뜻과 higher·lower를 연결해야 한다.

items.title: [1–10] Read the passage and answer the questions.
items.text:
People usually make tough decisions by voting for one of two or more options. The option that gets the most votes is the (a) ______. This is called majority rule. However, even if only 51% of people in a group vote for an option, ⟪they⟫ will get their choice. That means, almost half of the people in that group will not get their choice. In that case, is majority rule really fair?

Most democracies (b) ______ public officials through a majority vote. In a system with two political parties, a slim margin, such as 51% to 49%, can decide an election. In a system with more than two parties, less than 50% of voters could give one political party a victory. To ensure the fairness of majority rule, certain conditions must be met. First, people should be able to vote with secret ballots. Second, each person’s vote should be weighted equally. Finally, there have to be enough voters to make a majority vote truly fair.

When an election is won with less than 50% of the total votes, the winning party must consider the opinions of the other voters. This is because running a democracy should ensure equality for all citizens.
items.note: Words: tough decision = a hard choice · vote = choose by marking a paper · option = a choice · majority = more than half · democracy = a country where people vote for their leaders · public official = a person who works for the government · political party = a group of people who try to win elections · slim margin = a very small difference · victory = a win · ensure = make sure · condition = something that must be true · be met = be followed · secret ballot = voting where no one sees your choice · be weighted equally = count the same · consider = think about · opinion = what a person thinks · citizen = a person of a country · equality = everyone being treated the same

items.prompt: According to the passage, how do people usually make tough decisions?
items.explanation: [난이도 1·매우 쉬움 / 세부 사실] People usually make tough decisions by voting for one of two or more options.

items.prompt: According to the passage, what can decide an election in a two-party system?
choices: a slim margin, such as 51% to 49%
items.explanation: [난이도 1·매우 쉬움 / 세부 사실] In a system with two political parties, a slim margin, such as 51% to 49%, can decide an election.

items.explanation: [난이도 2·쉬움 / 문장 빈칸 어휘] 가장 많은 표를 얻은 선택지가 ‘승자(winner)’이고, 이것을 다수결이라 부른다. 바로 뒤에서 51%만 얻어도 ‘원하는 것을 얻는다(get their choice)’고 했다.

items.prompt: Which word best fits in blank (b)?
items.explanation: [난이도 2·쉬움 / 문장 빈칸 어휘] 민주주의 국가는 다수결 투표로 공직자를 ‘뽑는다(elect)’. 뒤 문장들이 모두 선거(election)와 표(votes) 이야기이다.

items.explanation: [난이도 5·어려움 / 추론·적용] 공정한 다수결의 세 조건: 비밀 투표(secret ballots), 모든 표가 같은 무게(weighted equally), 충분한 투표자(enough voters). ④만 세 조건을 모두 만족한다. 지도자 혼자 투표하거나 세 명만 투표하면 투표자가 부족하고, 모두가 볼 수 있으면 비밀 투표가 아니며, 어떤 표가 두 번 계산되면 표의 무게가 같지 않다.

items.prompt: What can we learn from the passage?

items.explanation: [난이도 5·어려움 / 추론] 두 정당 체제에서는 51% 대 49% 같은 근소한 차이로 결정되고(a slim margin … can decide), 50% 미만으로 이기는 경우는 ‘정당이 셋 이상인 체제’에서만 말했으므로, 두 정당 체제의 승자는 절반이 넘는 표를 얻는다고 추론할 수 있다. 선거는 근소한 차이로 결정될 수 있고(never close ✗), 49%는 지며, 공직자는 다수결 투표로 뽑는다.

items.title: [1–10] Read the passage and answer the questions.
items.text:
Throughout history, humans have looked at the stars as a map, as a guide, and for worship. The invention of the telescope has helped humans (a) ______. How have telescopes changed over time?

Telescopes were ⟪originally⟫ used to see long distances. Galileo was one of the first to use a telescope to observe the stars. His telescope used a concave eyepiece and a convex lens. This gave the image seen through the telescope an upright view and magnified it up to thirty times! Even though Galileo’s telescope was quite useful at the time, the images it produced were blurry. Kepler ⟪improved⟫ on Galileo’s design by using a convex eyepiece and lens. This gave a much wider field of view, even though the images appeared upside-down.

In modern times, telescopes have been launched into space to help astronomers observe (b) ______. One example is the Hubble Telescope, which orbits Earth and sends back high-quality pictures of distant planets and galaxies. Through continued technological developments, humans can understand the universe much better.
items.note: Words: worship = praying to a god · invention = making something new for the first time · observe = watch carefully · concave = curved in · convex = curved out · eyepiece = the part you look into · upright = with the top at the top (not upside-down) · magnify = make bigger · blurry = not clear · field of view = how much you can see · upside-down = the top at the bottom · launch = send into space · orbit = go around · distant = far away · galaxy = a very large group of stars · universe = everything in space · continued = going on · technological development = new technology

items.prompt: According to the passage, who was one of the first to use a telescope to observe the stars?
items.explanation: [난이도 1·매우 쉬움 / 세부 사실] Galileo was one of the first to use a telescope to observe the stars. Kepler는 그 설계를 개선한 사람이고, Hubble은 우주 망원경의 이름이다.

items.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Hubble Telescope send back?
items.explanation: [난이도 1·매우 쉬움 / 세부 사실] the Hubble Telescope, which orbits Earth and sends back high-quality pictures of distant planets and galaxies.

items.prompt: What does the underlined word ⟪originally⟫ mean?
items.explanation: [난이도 2·쉬움 / 어휘(단어 뜻)] originally(원래, 처음에는) = at first. 망원경은 ‘처음에는’ 먼 거리를 보는 데 쓰였다는 뜻이다.

items.prompt: What does the underlined word ⟪improved⟫ mean?
items.explanation: [난이도 2·쉬움 / 어휘(단어 뜻)] improve(개선하다) = make better. Kepler가 Galileo의 설계를 ‘더 좋게 만들었다’는 뜻으로, 뒤에 시야가 훨씬 넓어졌다는 설명이 이어진다.

items.prompt: Complete the table about the passage. Which words best fit (A) and (B)?
choices: (A) friend …… (B) the bottom of the sea
items.explanation: [난이도 3·보통 / 도표 완성] (A) humans have looked at the stars as a map, as a guide, and for worship — 별을 ‘지도(map)’로 삼았다. (B) Telescopes were originally used to see long distances — 망원경으로 ‘먼 거리(long distances)’를 볼 수 있었다.
table: People used the stars as a (A) ______ and a guide.

items.prompt:
Complete the summary of the passage. Which words best fit (A) and (B)?

Galileo’s telescope made the image (A) ______ and much bigger, but the image was (B) ______.
items.explanation: [난이도 3·보통 / 요약문 완성] (A) This gave the image … an upright view and magnified it up to thirty times — 이미지는 ‘똑바로(upright)’ 보였고 크게 확대되었다. (B) the images it produced were blurry — 하지만 ‘흐릿했다(blurry)’. 거꾸로 보인 것은 Kepler의 망원경이다.

items.prompt: What is paragraph 2 mainly about?
choices: the early telescopes of Galileo and Kepler
why the stars are far away
how the Hubble Telescope takes its pictures
items.explanation: [난이도 4·다소 어려움 / 문단 주제] 2문단은 Galileo 망원경(똑바로 선 상, 30배 확대, 흐릿함)과 이를 개선한 Kepler 망원경(넓은 시야, 거꾸로 된 상)을 설명한다. Hubble 망원경은 3문단의 내용이다.

items.prompt: What is paragraph 3 mainly about?
choices: what Galileo’s telescope was made of
telescopes in space, like the Hubble Telescope
items.explanation: [난이도 4·다소 어려움 / 문단 주제] 3문단은 우주로 발사된 현대 망원경, 특히 Hubble 망원경이 하는 일을 설명한다. 첫 망원경, Galileo 망원경의 렌즈, Kepler의 설계, 흐릿한 상은 2문단의 내용이다.

items.prompt: Which best fits in blank (a)?
choices: see and understand the stars better
see things that are close to them
items.explanation: [난이도 5·어려움 / 빈칸 추론] 사람들이 오랫동안 별을 바라봤고, 뒤 문단에서 망원경으로 별을 ‘관측하고(observe)’ 우주를 ‘더 잘 이해하게(understand the universe much better)’ 되었다고 했다. 따라서 망원경의 발명은 별을 ‘더 잘 보고 이해하도록’ 도운 것이다. 별로 날아가거나 지구의 지도를 만든다는 내용은 없고, 별에 기도한 것은 망원경 이전의 일이며, 망원경은 ‘먼 거리’를 보는 도구이다.

items.prompt: Which best fits in blank (b)?
choices: the stars and the whole universe
only the Moon and the Sun
the stars, but not the galaxies
items.explanation: [난이도 5·어려움 / 빈칸 추론] 바로 뒤 문장에서 Hubble 망원경이 ‘먼(distant)’ 행성과 ‘은하(galaxies)’의 사진을 보내온다고 했으므로, 우주 망원경은 별뿐 아니라 우주 전체를 관측하도록 돕는다. 가까운 별·행성만 본다거나, 달과 태양만 본다거나, 은하는 보지 않는다는 것은 이와 어긋난다.
